questions.q: Which table stores supplier-level procurement attributes, and what is its primary key?
questions.explain: POZ_SUPPLIERS stores supplier-level attributes with primary key VENDOR_ID, a naming holdover from Oracle's older terminology.

questions.q: Where does a supplier's actual name and core identity live?
options: Directly in a NAME column on POZ_SUPPLIERS
In HZ_PARTIES, joined through the PARTY_ID column on POZ_SUPPLIERS
Nowhere — supplier names are not stored
questions.explain: POZ_SUPPLIERS does not store the name directly; it carries a PARTY_ID foreign key into the shared HZ_PARTIES identity table.

options: Site-level supplier detail, such as pay-site and purchasing-site flags, keyed by VENDOR_SITE_ID
questions.explain: POZ_SUPPLIER_SITES_ALL_M holds site-level attributes like pay-site and purchasing-site flags, each row tied back to its supplier via VENDOR_ID.

questions.q: Where are a supplier's bank account details stored?
options: In Oracle Payments schema tables prefixed IBY_, such as IBY_EXT_BANK_ACCOUNTS
questions.explain: Bank account details live in the Oracle Payments (IBY_) schema, not directly on the supplier or supplier site tables.

questions.q: Why can a single supplier have one site marked as a valid pay site and a different site NOT marked as a valid purchasing site?
options: Because site-level flags like pay-site and purchasing-site are set independently per site row, not inherited from the supplier header
Because this is not possible — all sites share identical flags
Because POZ_SUPPLIERS overrides every site's flags
Because purchasing flags only exist on HZ_PARTIES
questions.explain: Pay-site and purchasing-site flags are set at the site level on POZ_SUPPLIER_SITES_ALL_M, so different sites under the same supplier can have different capabilities.
